ety.text: From Middle English seuen, sewen, siwen, borrowed from Anglo-Norman suer, siwer et al. and Old French sivre (“to follow after”) (modern French suivre), from Vulgar Latin *sequere (“to follow”), from Latin sequi. Cognate with Italian seguire and Spanish seguir. Doublet of segue. Related to suit.

senses.d: To file a legal action against someone, generally a non-criminal (civil) action.
ex: sue someone for selling a faulty product
I plan to sue you for everything you have.

senses.d: To seek by request; to make application; to petition; to entreat; to plead.
ex: The king of Bimsa sued for peace after Nynal's armies overran his territory; he knew any further resistance would only harm the common people.

senses.d: To leave high and dry on shore.

ex: And the olde knyght seyde unto the yonge knyght, ‘Sir, swith me.’
